title: When the word jazz came into use
summary: Spikes says jazz did not come into use until after World War I, crediting James Reese Europe's band; before that it was called ragtime.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You called it a jazz band. When was the first time you remember hearing the term "Jazz"? When did it come into the music?

I couldn't tell you that. It didn't come till after the war. It didn't come till after the war was over, and I think the first one...I think Europe* was the first one that...you know he had the jazz band. I think Europe was. You know he had a big band in the Army, and when he come back, they'd never had a big band that played that kind of music, and I think that's where he started. I think that's when they started to calling it jazz then. But before that, it was called "Ragtime." Yeah. And when you played hot stuff, they called it the blues, you know. But jazz, I don't think, was started till after the war.
I wondered, because when you said, "The jazz band..." I wondered if that term was used then.
No. It wasn't. They...we was just the...the
